category_title: Verbal students with autism who discuss negative topics and use headsets to avoid interaction
student_description: Jordan is a student who struggles with unstructured social interactions, often avoiding them by walking rapidly and wearing a headset, or engaging in repetitive, negative, and disturbing talk when he does interact. The evidence reveals he uniquely needs highly structured communication tools with visual symbols (due to limited reading skills), explicit step-by-step instruction in turn-taking, and prepared peer partners to successfully initiate and sustain reciprocal conversations.

criteria.rationale: Due to his limited reading skills, Jordan cannot rely on text alone and needs visual symbols to independently use communication tools.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must explicitly incorporate the use of visual supports (e.g., Picture Communication Symbols) alongside any text-based communication materials.

criteria.rationale: Jordan rarely sustains interactions on his own, so his peers must be explicitly prepared to understand his communication tools and ask reciprocal questions.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include a strategy for orienting, preparing, or training peers on how to interact with Jordan and respond to his communication book.

criteria.rationale: To move beyond scripted interactions and prevent a return to repetitive negative topics, Jordan must eventually learn to generate novel responses.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include goals or methods for teaching Jordan to ask follow-up or novel questions based on his peers' responses.
